disclaimer: Facts are reported as stated by named sources, with links. This is information, not investment, legal or credit advice, and not a rating of any company. Confidence labels describe how well we have documented a fact, not anyone's finances.

claims.statement: The Texas Tribune reports Gov. Abbott announced on 2026-08-03 a moratorium on new data centers connecting to the state grid, and ordered ERCOT to require developers to provide information on tax breaks, power use, water, community impact and ownership.
claims.source_name: Texas Tribune

claims.statement: The Texas Tribune reports Gov. Abbott directed the Texas Water Development Board on 2026-09-15 to penalize data centers that fail to report water use; only 28% had answered a mandatory survey.
claims.source_name: Texas Tribune

claims.statement: The Texas Tribune reports Gov. Abbott ordered the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality on 2026-09-21 to stop issuing environmental permits for data centers until audits are complete. No end date was given.
claims.source_name: Texas Tribune

claims.statement: Data Center Watch (10a Labs), as relayed by Gizmodo, counted 75 projects worth about $130 billion blocked or delayed in Q1 2026.
claims.source_name: Gizmodo

claims.statement: Data Center Watch (10a Labs), as relayed by Gizmodo, counted 45 projects worth about $68 billion blocked or delayed from April to June 2026.
claims.source_name: Gizmodo

claims.statement: SemiAnalysis argues most projects flagged as 'canceled' are early-stage ones without site control, financing or interconnection. It says its 2026 North America hyperscaler self-build forecast moved only about 1%, and colocation under 5%, over six months.
claims.source_name: SemiAnalysis

claims.statement: The dcmap.us tracker lists 56 formal public actions across 25 states (22 statewide, 34 local), with entries through August 2026.
claims.source_name: dcmap.us: US Data Center Policy Tracker

claims.statement: Gallup, in a poll fielded 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-18 (1,000 adults, margin of error about 4 points), found 71% oppose construction of AI data centers in their local area and 27% favor. 48% strongly oppose.
claims.source_name: Gallup: Americans Oppose AI Data Centers in Their Area

claims.statement: The UMass Amherst Poll, fielded 2026-08-21 to 2026-08-26 (1,000 respondents, margin of error 3.5 points), found 65% oppose, 11% support and 24% neither, when asked about an AI data center in their local community.
claims.source_name: UMass Amherst Poll (Sept 2026 national)

claims.statement: Embold Research, for Heatmap, fielded 2026-08-08 to 2026-08-13 (2,045 registered voters, margin of error 2.3 points) and found 75% would oppose a data center built near their home, 61% strongly (per Heatmap News).
claims.source_name: Heatmap News: Embold Research poll

claims.statement: Heatmap's four polls show opposition rising from 42% (Aug 2025, with 43% in support) to 51% (Feb 2026), 70% (May 2026) and 75% (Aug 2026), per Heatmap News.
claims.source_name: Heatmap News: Embold Research poll

claims.statement: Ballotpedia counts 38 data-center-related ballot measures in eight states in 2026, including 20 in Ohio across 17 jurisdictions. 34 of the 38 are on the 2026-11-03 ballot. In the four earlier 2026 votes, voters favored greater restrictions each time.
claims.source_name: Ballotpedia News: data center ballot measures

claims.statement: Seward & Kissel reports that on 2026-07-29 the SEC's Office of Structured Finance issued guidance that certain data center securitizations, where a bankruptcy-remote issuer owns or controls the facilities, are not 'asset-backed securities' under Exchange Act Section 3(a)(79), because the collateral is non-self-liquidating. Securities Act and other requirements still apply.
claims.original_reporter: SEC Office of Structured Finance (per Seward & Kissel)
claims.source_name: Seward & Kissel: SEC data center securitization guidance

claims.statement: EEI's list, dated 2026-09-11, catalogs publicly announced large-load projects of about 20 MW or more, totaling more than $1.13 trillion of investment and more than 71 GW of connected load. It says 32 states have approved large-load tariffs and 7 more are pending.
claims.source_name: EEI: Large Load Projects and Tariffs (Sept 2026)

claims.statement: CoBank, describing the SEPA and NCCETC DELTa database, says a common large-load rate design has emerged: contracts of 10 to 20 years, minimum bills of about 70 to 100% of contracted capacity, and collateral and exit rules.
claims.source_name: SEPA and NCCETC: DELTa large-load tariff database

claims.statement: A JPMorgan analysis from May 2026, relayed by Moneywise, says 60% of data center capacity meant to be completed by 2027 has not reached the construction stage, and another 7% is delayed.
claims.source_name: Moneywise: IMF and JPMorgan on AI data center debt

claims.statement: Per Moneywise, the IMF's Tobias Adrian warned of "a potential maturity mismatch in between the duration of the physical assets and the duration of the debt."
claims.source_name: Moneywise: IMF and JPMorgan on AI data center debt

claims.statement: CBRE says U.S. data center vacancy hit a record low of 1.4% in H1 2026 (0.2% in Northern Virginia), and that 80.4% of under-construction capacity is already preleased.
claims.source_name: CBRE: North America Data Center Trends H1 2026

claims.statement: CBRE says under-construction capacity rose 24.8% to a record 7,481.1 MW, with Atlanta (2,882 MW) overtaking Northern Virginia as the top construction market.
claims.source_name: CBRE: North America Data Center Trends H1 2026

claims.statement: CBRE writes that "the ability to secure local approval has become as critical to site selection as power and fiber availability," and that power availability and infrastructure delivery timelines remain the most decisive siting factors.
claims.source_name: CBRE: North America Data Center Trends H1 2026

claims.statement: Bank of America's Karen Fang told Bloomberg: "Readiness means all the permitting and approvals that are required, and the community support."
claims.original_reporter: Bank of America (Karen Fang, per Bloomberg)
claims.source_name: Bloomberg via BNN: lenders scrutinize data center financing

claims.statement: Bloomberg reports that banks including JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America and KKR Capital Markets are weighing community opposition and project readiness in credit decisions, favoring welcoming states and asking for community-engagement documentation.
claims.source_name: Bloomberg via BNN: lenders scrutinize data center financing

claims.statement: A Bloom Energy and Latitude Media survey of 156 industry respondents found 51% name power availability as a top-three concern, down from 84% in June 2025, and 28% say community opposition has worsened in the past six months.
claims.original_reporter: Bloom Energy and Latitude Media survey
claims.source_name: Bloom Energy and Latitude Media: Data Center Power Report 2026

claims.statement: Urban Land, citing Bloomberg, reports local opposition has stalled or blocked at least 48 U.S. data center projects (about $156 billion), that cancellations rose from 6 in 2024 to 25 in 2025, and that about 188 local groups operate in 40 states.
claims.source_name: Urban Land Institute: The Rising Cost of Data Center Pushback

claims.statement: ComputeLaw reports the U.S. had 159 million fiber miles in 2024, projected to reach 373 million by 2029, and that long-haul route miles are expected to grow from 95,000 to 187,000.
claims.source_name: ComputeLaw: long-haul and middle-mile fiber

claims.statement: ComputeLaw reports NTIA's Middle Mile Program has awarded $980 million to 36 organizations to fund more than 12,500 miles of new middle-mile fiber.
claims.source_name: ComputeLaw: long-haul and middle-mile fiber

claims.statement: POWER magazine, citing a Wood Mackenzie Q2 2025 survey, reports lead times of 128 weeks for power transformers, 144 weeks for generator step-up units, and 44 weeks for switchgear.
claims.source_name: POWER magazine: transformers in 2026

claims.statement: POWER magazine, citing Wood Mackenzie, reports a 30% supply deficit for power transformers and 10% for distribution transformers in 2025, with power transformer demand up 119% and prices up 77% since 2019, and data centers named as a major driver.
claims.source_name: POWER magazine: transformers in 2026

claims.statement: ITIF, citing a Wall Street Journal article of 2025-11-29, says the construction industry faced a 439,000-worker shortage driven by data center growth, and that data center construction roles pay up to 30% more than typical construction jobs.
claims.source_name: ITIF: construction worker shortage

discrepancies.description: Time News and the Texas Tribune both report Texas action on data centers. The Tribune gives dated orders: grid connections (2026-08-03), water reporting (2026-09-15) and environmental permits (2026-09-21). The governor's own orders have not yet been pulled.
discrepancies.what_would_settle_it: Governor's office press releases or executive orders; TCEQ and ERCOT notices.

discrepancies.description: Reports differ on how much capacity is really affected. Data Center Watch counts projects blocked or delayed by opposition. SemiAnalysis says most 'canceled' projects were early-stage and never had 2026 commitments. The two may count different things.
discrepancies.what_would_settle_it: Read both methodologies; compare project lists.

discrepancies.description: The polls agree on direction but differ on level. Gallup found 71% oppose and 27% favor; UMass found 65% oppose, 11% support and 24% neither. The UMass question offered a 'neither' option, which can lower measured opposition. Dates, wording and methods also differ.
discrepancies.what_would_settle_it: Compare exact questions and response options across the polls.

discrepancies.description: The SEC guidance on data center securitizations is known only through a law firm's summary. The staff guidance itself has not yet been pulled.

Counts of projects hit by local opposition differ. Data Center Watch counts 75 projects (about $130 billion) blocked or delayed in Q1 2026 alone. A Bloomberg count cited by Urban Land says at least 48 projects (about $156 billion) stalled or blocked. Periods and definitions differ.
discrepancies.what_would_settle_it: Compare the two methodologies and project lists.
